Two governments described the same explosions on Saturday and their stories don't match.

Iran's Revolutionary Guard says missiles and drones hit radars at two bases, and Bahrain says a civilian industrial site burned with nobody hurt.

Lt. Col. Anthony Aguilar, a retired Green Beret officer, thinks both versions can be true.

He says the radars that feed Patriot batteries ride on trailers and fold up small enough to park almost anywhere, and that on his own deployments he saw them set up outside bases, though nothing shows that happened here.

What worries him more is what Tehran kept in the garage:

"Iran is still not even getting into its good stuff. This is the small stuff."

Iran now says any American drone over its territory gets answered with a strike on a base.

How many radars can the Gulf lose before a real missile wave shows up with nobody watching?
